iterations.theme: The Return of Avangarda, the New Album, and Collaboration with Krešo Bengalka

sections.subtitle: The Return of the Hip Hop Duo Avangarda to the New Season of the Ril Tok Podcast
sections.screenshot_description: Hosts Khan and Doktor Oga greet the guests from the hip hop group Avangarda in the studio
sections.content:
The jubilee 202nd episode of the **Ril Tok Podcast** began in a relaxed tone, with standard jokes from the hosting duo consisting of **Khan** and **Doktor Oga**. After a brief review of the sponsors and technical details regarding the new season, the hosts proudly announced the return of guests who, in Khan's words, represent the very top of the domestic underground hip hop scene – the duo **Avangarda** (Leon and Dejan).

After almost three and a half years since their first guest appearance, the guys from Avangarda once again sat down at the podcast table to present their new, long-awaited material. Khan emphasized that the new album is his personal favorite, while the guests commented with a smile that the success of new releases is traditionally celebrated in the late night hours at gas stations, happy to be back in the studio with the crew.

sections.subtitle: Explosion of Numbers and First Reactions to the New Project
sections.screenshot_description: Members of Avangarda speak about the spike in listenership on Spotify after the release of the album
sections.content:
The conversation soon turned to the first impressions and audience reactions after the new album saw the light of day. A guest from Avangarda revealed an interesting statistical piece of data that best illustrates the listeners' interest: in just a month, the number of monthly listeners on the **Spotify** platform jumped from an initial 200 to more than 3,700.

Although they emphasize that numbers themselves are neither their primary motive nor their ultimate goal, the band members admit that such a jump is a great wind at their back for a project that was created over more than three years. The work process began back at the end of 2021 and the beginning of 2022, and the release of the album marked the culmination of a long and carefully planned creative process.

sections.subtitle: Evolution of Sound: A Departure from the Drumless Aesthetic with Flow Deep's Production Signature
sections.screenshot_description: Guests analyze the change in sound and the collaboration with producer Flow Deep
sections.content:
One of the key topics of the conversation was the noticeable evolution in Avangarda's soundscape. While their earlier works were deeply rooted in raw boom bap and the so-called 'drumless' style – a sound that many associate with the popular movement led by the **Griselda** label – the new album brings a significantly more dynamic and modern arrangement.

The members of Avangarda point out that working on 'drumless' beats was the perfect training ground for honing lyrical skills because it leaves the most room for complex rhymes and wordplay. However, saturation with that style prompted them to make a step forward. A key role in that transition was played by producer **Flow Deep**, who became a kind of third member of the team. Together they created a sound that draws its roots from the hip hop of the 2000s, with more massive rhythms and more energetic production that communicates far more easily with the audience at live performances.

sections.subtitle: Music Created for the Car and the Gym
sections.screenshot_description: Doktor Oga and the guests comment on how the new rhythms perfectly suit workouts and driving
sections.content:
Co-host Doktor Oga shared his experience, emphasizing that he listened to the entire album in the gym and that the rhythm of the songs perfectly raises energy during strength training and running. The guests agreed with that remark, emphasizing that this was precisely one of their primary goals when choosing beats.

They wanted to create music that 'works' in the car, where the bass and dynamics make the listener roll down the windows and turn the volume all the way up. Contrary to previous releases that were more intimate and suitable for home listening, the new arrangements carry a strong club and concert charge, giving the songs full intensity regardless of whether they are listened to on headphones or a sound system.

sections.subtitle: Collective Work, Lyrical Standards, and Recognizable Chemistry
sections.screenshot_description: Leon and Dejan speak about writing lyrics together and complementing each other
sections.content:
Speaking about the creative process, the guests explained that they functioned more harmoniously on this project than ever before. While earlier they often wrote separate verses of 16 bars each and joined them in the studio, the new album is the fruit of working together on the spot. They divided verses in half, alternated bar for bar, and jointly refined each rhyme in order to achieve maximum fluidity.

Khan noted that the duo functions like a single unit in which contrasting vocals and performance styles perfectly complement each other. The members of Avangarda add that they took care that the lyrics remain uncompromising and humorous, but also thematically accessible, refusing to pander to commercial trends at the expense of their own lyrical identity.

sections.subtitle: Studio Perfectionism and the Quest for the Ideal Chorus
sections.screenshot_description: Band members describe the lengthy work on choruses and collaboration in the studio
sections.content:
One of the biggest challenges during recording was shaping memorable, more melodic choruses. The guest from Avangarda admitted that they recorded and altered certain choruses for months – sometimes more than half a year would pass until they reached the final version with which both of them, together with Flow Deep, were completely satisfied.

Although in hip hop there is a fine line between a natural moment and excessive nitpicking, Avangarda insisted on perfectionism. Experimenting with new vocal lines and melodies brought additional freshness to the songs, and the final result justified the hours spent in studio work.

sections.subtitle: Collaboration with the Split Icon: How the Song 'Nani' with Krešo Bengalka Came to Be
sections.screenshot_description: Guests recount the anecdote about sending a message and the quick recording of the collaboration with Krešo Bengalka
sections.content:
Special emphasis was placed on the song **'Nani'**, which features one of the most recognizable names in regional hip hop – **Krešo Bengalka**. The guests revealed that they weighed for a long time whom to invite as guests on the album and initially considered several options on the planning board, but Krešo emerged as the ideal choice for the raw energy of that specific track.

Although they had a certain amount of stage fright about whether the collaboration would happen at all because they did not know each other personally, Krešo Bengalka reacted extremely quickly and professionally. After they sent him the working version, the Split rapper recorded and sent his part within two days, and an impressive verse of as many as 24 bars instead of the standard 16 at that. Khan praised Krešo's status as the 'king of guest appearances' on the domestic scene, while the guys from Avangarda concluded that this collaboration also carried special emotional weight for them given that they grew up listening to his work.

iterations.theme: Anecdotes, TLC Festival at the Garden, and Club Promotion

sections.subtitle: Neighborhood Ties and a Relaxed Atmosphere: How Split 3 and Beer Marked the Hangout in the Studio
sections.screenshot_description: Host Khan and the members of Avangarda discuss neighborhood anecdotes in the studio over beer.
sections.content:
The conversation in the *Ril Tok* podcast studio takes on an extremely casual and friendly tone when a new round of beer is ordered, and host Khan and members of the duo Avangarda (Leon and Dejan) begin a discussion about neighborhood roots. The focus turned to the fact that one of the members of Avangarda shares a common Split neighborhood with Krešo Bengalka – the well-known Split 3.

Through laughter and relaxed ribbing, they recall the specific architecture of Split 3, the gigantic buildings, and the iconic neighborhood atmosphere of the 1970s. Host Khan wittily observes that in such an environment every hangout naturally gravitates toward long late-night conversations and anecdotes from gas stations.

sections.subtitle: The Cult T-shirt of Kiša metaka, Spilled Acetone, and Memories of Zagreb Beginnings
sections.screenshot_description: The guest gestures and recounts the anecdote about the destruction of the first Kiša metaka T-shirt.
sections.content:
One of the most entertaining moments of the episode brings an anecdote about coming to Zagreb in 2013 and buying the first official T-shirt of the cult Split hip-hop group Kiša metaka after a gig at KSET. The guest recalls how at that time Vojko V called him directly on his cell phone because the postman could not locate him at his grandmother's address, which gave the entire purchase a special charm.

However, the fate of the first T-shirt ended ingloriously in the bathroom. The guest describes in detail the bizarre moment when a bottle of acetone tipped over from the edge of the sink, fell onto the toilet bowl where the laid-aside T-shirt was sitting, and permanently damaged it. Despite holes and stains, the T-shirt was never thrown away – today it has relic status and serves as a chair cover, reminding of formative days and eternal respect for the work of their Split colleagues.

sections.subtitle: Degustation of Pomalo Beer: From Cheap Bagged Wine to Craft Culture
sections.screenshot_description: The crew in the studio toasts with Pomalo craft beer and recalls their youthful nights out.
sections.content:
Opening bottles of Pomalo craft beer triggered a wave of nostalgia for nights out during high school and university days. While Doktor Oga and Khan taste and praise the flavor of the domestic craft beer, the guests recall their youthful graduation celebrations (norijade) and park drinks that left lasting consequences on their generation's stomachs.

Notorious drinks from their early party days came up for discussion – from 'Vigor' and cheap pelinkovac to cult wines in a bag and Tetra Pak like 'Ribar' and 'Vranac'. The interlocutors conclude through laughter that it is a real miracle they survived those 'dark nights' and park tussles, and observe that today's transition to quality craft beer is proof not only of maturity, but also of sheer survival instinct.

sections.subtitle: Exclusive Avangarda Merch: Limited Edition, Heavy Cotton, and Flawless Design
sections.screenshot_description: Host Khan proudly shows off the new black Avangarda T-shirt in front of the cameras.
sections.content:
After stories about old T-shirts, exclusive merch from the group Avangarda itself arrives in the studio. The guests handed the hosts copies from a strictly limited series of only 30 pieces, made on the occasion of promoting the new album.

Khan and Doktor Oga did not hide their enthusiasm for the quality of the material. It is a heavy, thicker cotton with a reinforced stiff collar and a modern oversize cut that perfectly fits the aesthetic of contemporary streetwear style. It was pointed out that the band did not want to make cheap compromises, but rather aimed for a top-quality product that fans will proudly wear for years.

sections.subtitle: Scene Reactions to the Stylistic Turn: 'We Didn't Sell Out, We Just Expanded the Playground'
sections.screenshot_description: Leon and Dejan discuss how the audience received the departure from classic boom-bap.
sections.content:
The release of the new material marked a noticeable stylistic shift compared to Avangarda's earlier releases. Instead of strictly sticking to the 'drumless' aesthetic and dark underground sound often associated with the Griselda label, the new album brings more dynamic rhythms, catchier choruses, and production that functions just as well in a car with rolled-down windows as on a club sound system.

Dejan and Leon emphasize that during work on the album they deliberately played tracks for friends who do not listen to rap at all, wanting to see a raw, unfiltered reaction. The response was extremely positive – the audience recognized the energy without feeling that the band lost its lyrical sharpness or compromised underground integrity.

sections.subtitle: Flow Deep's Production Vision and Nota Limun's Unwavering Contribution
sections.screenshot_description: Conversation about the importance of Flow Deep as executive producer and arranger on the project.
sections.content:
In creating the overall sonic identity of the new project, producer Flow Deep played a key role. The members of Avangarda explain that Flow Deep was not just a beatmaker who sends beats, but a real executive producer who filtered ideas, discarded what was unnecessary, and pushed them out of their comfort zone.

Special emphasis was placed on the collaboration with Nota Limun on the track 'Bagra protiv sebe'. The crew has only words of praise for Nota Limun, pointing out his recognizable energy and brutal guest verses with which he regularly elevates every song to a new level. With a dose of humor, his temporary move to Zagreb's Retkovec was also mentioned, by which he additionally strengthened ties with the local scene.

sections.subtitle: TLC Block Party at the Garden: Bringing Foreign Performers and the Reality of Organization
sections.screenshot_description: The interlocutors analyze organizational challenges and the atmosphere at the performance in The Garden Brewery.
sections.content:
The central concert topic was this year's TLC event held at The Garden Brewery, which by its concept was conceived as a real all-day 'block party' with graffiti, table tennis, and various outdoor activities. Avangarda performed before a numerous domestic audience, confirming the status of one of the most sought-after underground names.

However, bringing foreign headliner Rigz brought certain organizational complications and delays, which prompted a broader discussion about how ready the domestic scene is for international names. Khan and the guests analyze the financial and logistical challenges of organizing such guest appearances, mentioning that in the future it would be worthwhile to target names like Lloyd Banks or Conway the Machine that carry stronger weight among regional hip-hop fans.

sections.subtitle: Club Promotion in Lođa: Intimate Moments and Fellowship That Keeps the Scene Alive
sections.screenshot_description: Dejan and Leon speak about the energy at the club promotion of the album in the Lođa venue.
sections.content:
As a complete contrast to large festival stages, members of Avangarda speak with particular passion about the club promotion of the album held at the cult Lođa. The venue, which has for years been the gathering base for the Zagreb hip-hop community, offered an intimate, packed atmosphere in which the boundary between performer and audience is erased.

Along with the sale of new merch and the support of colleagues who exhibited their works and props, the evening passed in jointly rapping verses just a few centimeters from the crowd. For Avangarda, precisely these kinds of so-called 'cozy' moments represent the very core of hip-hop culture – raw energy, direct exchange of respect, and the feeling of creating for people who truly understand every spoken rhyme.

iterations.theme: The Concert Scene, Announcement of Vintage, and Dissecting Key Tracks

sections.subtitle: Concert Autumn in the Region: From Historical Legends to the Raw Griselda Sound
sections.screenshot_description: Khan and the members of Avangarda enthusiastically discuss upcoming hip-hop concerts in Zagreb and Ljubljana.
sections.content:
In a review of upcoming hip-hop events in the region, host Khan opened the topic of the rich concert offer awaiting domestic fans of the genre. Various names came up for discussion – from pioneers of hip-hop culture such as Grandmaster Flash, who is performing at Ljubljana's Gala Hala and then at Zagreb's Boogaloo, to neo-soul and hip-hop performers such as Bilal. The participants in the discussion also touched upon domestic club programs and performances by artists such as Edo Maajka and the joint performance by TBF and The Bastardz at Boćarski dom.

However, the biggest wave of excitement in the studio was caused by the announcement of American rapper Conway the Machine coming to Zagreb. Khan and the members of Avangarda spared no words of praise for the New York artist, highlighting his flawless live performance technique. Dejan and Leon emphasize that at concerts Conway literally does not miss a single line, maintaining an incredible tempo without losing his breath even when performing some fifteen songs in a row solo. In addition, they praised the organizers' decision to set up the Zagreb collective Scripta & Friends as domestic support and warm-up, which they consider a superb move for domestic rappers of a similar stylistic orientation.

sections.subtitle: Unexpected Surprise in the Studio and Scheduling a Solo Triumph at Vintage
sections.screenshot_description: Host Khan hands concert tickets to the members of Avangarda while they announce their big performance.
sections.content:
After the guests admitted that due to obligations and constant postponement they almost ended up without tickets for the Zagreb performance of Conway the Machine, a surprise followed. Khan, in cooperation with partners, secured tickets for both members of Avangarda, thereby resolving their worry about going to the concert of their favorite artist, along with an agreement to hang out together at the event.

The conversation about concerts served as a perfect overture to the key news: Avangarda officially announced their big solo, full-evening concert at Zagreb's Vintage Industrial Bar, scheduled for February 11. Unlike previous shorter festival and club sets, the duo is preparing an extensive repertoire lasting an hour and a half to two hours, with numerous guests and a dissection of their entire discography. Dejan and Leon emphasize that Vintage Industrial Bar is one of the best Zagreb venues precisely because of professional sound and superb stage conditions, adding that the right time has come to crown their work so far with a grand solo spectacle.

sections.subtitle: From Khan's Home Studio to Indian Streets: Beginnings and Unusual Experiences
sections.screenshot_description: Dejan and Leon evoke memories through laughter about their first recorded songs and specific life stages.
sections.content:
The conversation veered into nostalgic waters with recollections of the very beginnings of Avangarda's collaboration with Khan. The guests recalled through laughter their first arrivals at Khan's home studio almost fifteen years ago, describing the workspace atmosphere, specific studio rules, and situations where lyrics had to be precisely rehearsed down to the last syllable. It was precisely those early recordings that marked their tempering in the domestic underground community.

As one of the most interesting digressions, the four-year stay of one of the band members in India was highlighted. Khan described this as a completely atypical move for someone from the scene, considering that young people from the region mostly go West in search of a standard of living, while the Indian experience represented a completely different kind of school of life. The guest described returning to India with his wife years later and the incredible contrasts and anecdotes with the local population, emphasizing that those authentic life experiences permanently influenced his worldview and the themes of his lyrics.

sections.subtitle: Doktor Asks: Focus on Visualization and Filming a Music Video for the Hit with Krešo Bengalka
sections.screenshot_description: Co-host Doktor Oga asks questions about planned music videos as part of his author's segment.
sections.content:
In the recognizable segment 'Doktor pita', co-host Doktor Oga confronted the guests with a question about visual plans for the new album. Having learned from the experience with their first two projects on which, by their own admission, they fell short in terms of continuity of releasing music videos, the members of Avangarda decisively announced a turnaround. The plan is to film at least five to six videos so that the material gains full momentum and adequate presence on digital platforms.

Priority in the screen-adaptation plan belongs to the song 'Nani', created in collaboration with Split rapper Krešo Bengalka. Immediately upon release, that song attracted significant public attention, and the guys revealed that the script is already in preparation and that they are soon starting to shoot the scenes. They promised a significantly higher production level and a more creative approach, noting that visual content must no longer lag behind the musical quality they achieved in the studio.

sections.subtitle: The End of the Myth About Creating 'Only for Oneself': Why Visual Identity Is Crucial for a Rapper
sections.screenshot_description: Khan and the guests discuss ego, the importance of music videos, and artistic ambitions in modern rap.
sections.content:
The topic of music videos opened a wider debate about the performer's visual identity and the modern way of consuming music. Khan and the members of Avangarda agreed with the assertion that today's music is watched just as much as it is listened to, which is why passivity regarding videos is fatal for any serious artist. The guys revealed that they invested in their own film camera (Lumix GH series) to gain the freedom to document their own performances and shoot guerrilla videos without waiting for external collaborators.

They directed particularly sharp criticism at the widespread attitude among certain musicians who claim that they 'create exclusively for themselves and their bedroom'. Khan and the guests consider such statements dishonest, emphasizing that rap is in its essence a competitive, ego-driven genre in which every artist intimately wants their work to reach as wide a circle of people as possible. Acknowledging one's own ambitions and taking control over visual identity were marked as a key sign of authorial maturity.

sections.subtitle: Emotional Anatomy of the Album: The Melancholy of 'Klub 27' and a Dedication to 'Propali sportaši'
sections.screenshot_description: Members of Avangarda analyze the message and emotion of their most important songs from the new album.
sections.content:
In the closing part of the conversation, the interlocutors dissected the most impressive tracks from the new release. A special place is held by the song 'Klub 27', which the authors knew immediately upon creation had to function as the album's outro. Unlike hard, energetic club numbers, that track brings raw emotionality, confrontation with impermanence, and a sort of catharsis after years spent on the scene. Dejan and Leon pointed out that it was precisely that song that evoked the deepest reactions from listeners who are otherwise not primarily tied to the rap genre.

Alongside 'Klub 27', they touched in detail upon the title concept of 'Propali sportaši' and the track 'Taj lik'. They explained that the title carries a bittersweet dedication to generations from the neighborhood who had potential, but ended up in other life struggles, drawing a parallel with cult works by Kiša metaka such as the song 'Konan'. They concluded that real rap lies precisely in the ability to convey imperfect, real life stories without false embellishment, which gives their new material lasting weight.

iterations.theme: Album Cover, Roots at Mac's, Domestic Hip-hop Beef, and Sign-off

sections.subtitle: Technical Corner and Working with Tusta: How the Striking Album Cover Came to Be
sections.screenshot_description: Members of Avangarda explain the photography process for the cover and the collaboration with Tusta.
sections.content:
In the continuation of the segment in which Doktor Oga questions the guests, the topic shifted to the technical and visual aspects of the new material. To the question about the equipment with which they record videos and shots themselves, the guests joke about various brands before confirming that they acquired a Lumix GH5 camera in order to have complete freedom in creating visual content. They point out that having their own camera allows them experimentation and independence, but for key projects they still choose to work with professionals.

They specifically touched upon the creation of the cover for the new album, which was entrusted to photographer Tusta. The members of Avangarda spoke with great respect about Tusta's professionalism and the atmosphere he creates on set. They described him as an expert who knows exactly what he is doing with lighting and composition, and who with his energy and approach creates immense comfort for the performers. After several hours of work, they were so motivated that they wanted to immediately continue with shooting new projects. Unlike the usual abstract graphics or random shots, for this album they decided to put their own faces on the cover, inspired by classic releases of hip-hop greats, aware that at this stage of their career the audience must know exactly who stands behind the flawless rhymes.

sections.subtitle: Ego and the Myth About Creating 'Only for Oneself': Why Real Rappers Want an Audience
sections.screenshot_description: Khan and the members of Avangarda discuss ego and honesty toward the audience in rap.
sections.content:
The conversation then deepened into the philosophy of rapping and the eternal dilemma around creating music 'for oneself' versus creating for the audience. Khan openly stated his view that he does not believe the stories of artists who claim that they make music solely for their own pleasure and without any desire for external recognition. He emphasized that every artist who publishes songs on platforms like YouTube and shares them on social media actually wants people to hear them, and the myth of modesty often falls apart the moment an opportunity for success or money comes along.

The guests from Avangarda completely agreed with that thesis, emphasizing that rap is by definition a competitive and egotistical genre. They admit that lyrics stem from personal lived situations in which ego plays a large role. They conclude that there is nothing wrong with an artist proudly standing behind their work and admitting that they want to reach as many people as possible. While their first album was strictly intended for a narrow circle of underground admirers, and the second was a transitional experiment, with the third release they consciously aim for a broader audience, while maintaining uncompromising lyrical sharpness.

sections.subtitle: Battle of the Trilogies: Will 'Propali sportaši 3' or 'Krv, znoj i suze 3' Come Out First?
sections.screenshot_description: Doktor Oga and Khan enter into a witty battle of wits over Khan's cult series.
sections.content:
In the continuation of the segment, Doktor Oga posed the question of whether Avangarda plans to complete the trilogy and release the project *Propali sportaši 3*. The question immediately sparked a dynamic and humorous discussion because it connected to Khan's earlier announcements about possible work on his own legendary album *Krv, znoj i suze 3*. A friendly dispute arose over whose trilogy carries greater weight on the scene and who will realize the third part first.

Doktor Oga poked Khan with the question of whether he made the first part of his cult series 'for himself' or for the audience, which caused loud laughter in the studio. Khan admitted that this album was a turning point in his career and a project into which he invested everything he had in order to achieve a notable impact. Dejan and Leon from Avangarda confirmed that they definitely plan to make the third installment of *Propali sportaši*, emphasizing that they hope their series will in time gain the status and respect enjoyed on the scene by Khan's work. They agreed that work on third parts requires absolute maturity, time, and a flawless selection of collaborators.

sections.subtitle: Beginnings at Red Records: Recalling the Mixing of the First Album at Mac's
sections.screenshot_description: Khan and the guests evoke memories of the Red Records studio and producer Mac.
sections.content:
Speaking about their roots and discographic path, members of Avangarda recalled the creation of their first album *Propali sportaši*, which was mixed at the well-known Red Records studio by producer Mac. At that time, Leon was living in India, and Dejan traveled to Sesvetski Kraljevec, specifically Kobiljak, in order to bring the material to completion. That anecdote reminded everyone present of the dedication and effort that were required for recording and mixing in the early stages of their career.

Khan also recalled his early days and recording in Mac's Geto Production studio in Dugo Selo, emphasizing that he was probably among the first clients. The interlocutors unanimously praised Mac as one of the key figures and 'good spirits' of domestic hip-hop. They highlighted his dedication to professional audio equipment, exceptional meticulousness in vocal mixing, and human warmth. Khan emphasized that passing through Mac's studio was an unavoidable step and a sort of school through which anyone seriously building a name on the Croatian rap scene had to pass.

sections.subtitle: Commentary on the Current Domestic Beef: The Clash Between Magellan and Burky
sections.screenshot_description: Khan and Dejan comment on the first round and diss tracks in the clash between Magellan and Burky.
sections.content:
One of the most interesting topics of the very finale of the show was the current clash on the domestic scene between Magellan (Špica) and Burky. Khan emphasized that a real rap beef had not happened on the scene for a long time and asked for the guests' honest opinion about the first round of exchanged diss tracks. Given that both actors are experienced names with long-standing tenure, the expectations of the audience and colleagues were exceptionally high.

Dejan gave a very direct and objective analysis. He praised Magellan, pointing out that he sounded exceptionally energetic, aggressive, and fresh, like his form in his best days. On the other hand, regarding Burky's response, he asserted that it was too lukewarm and restrained for the standards Burky normally sets. They singled out the line about 'bocadillos' as convincingly the strongest moment of Burky's track, but agreed that the entire song should have been filled with such killer punchlines instead of general rhymes. Khan agreed with that assessment, adding that these are stylistically equal rappers and that in the first round Magellan took a clear lead.

sections.subtitle: Boxing Match with a Microphone: Analysis of Styles and Predictions for the Continuation of the Clash
sections.screenshot_description: Participants discuss whether the beef will continue with new songs.
sections.content:
In the continuation of dissecting the conflict, Khan and the crew discussed whether this beef was concluded or if it was merely the calm before the storm. They drew interesting boxing parallels, comparing their showdown to matches between heavyweights like Mike Tyson and Evander Holyfield, emphasizing that more mature rappers carry with them a specific weight and authority that younger performers often lack.

Doktor Oga posed the question of whether anyone knows the real reason why Magellan initiated the diss in the first place, to which the guests replied jokingly that he might have simply wanted to 'stir up' the atmosphere a bit on a scene that had been dormant for too long. Khan expressed his conviction that the clash is not over yet. He believes that Magellan could drop another response if he senses that Burky is again preparing material, while Burky, after analyzing the audience reactions, could strike back with considerably harder and more precise punches. They concluded that this kind of competitive fire benefits the scene immensely because it awakens the audience and serves as a reminder of the fundamental tenets of hip-hop culture.

sections.subtitle: Closing Messages and Sign-off: Announcement of the Big Concert at Vintage and Greetings to the Viewers
sections.screenshot_description: The podcast crew toasts and signs off the 202nd episode of Ril Tok with greetings to the audience.
sections.content:
After more than two and a half hours of intense and entertaining conversation, the 202nd episode of the Ril Tok Podcast was brought to a close. Hosts Khan and Doktor Oga left the final word to the guests from Avangarda. Dejan and Leon expressed their gratitude for the warm hospitality, praised the crew's professionalism and the humorous segment 'Doktor pita', and expressed hope for another meeting in the studio.

Khan once again reminded the audience to listen to the new album *Propali sportaši 2* on all streaming services and announced their big solo concert scheduled for February 11, 2027 at Vintage Industrial Bar, as well as attending together the Zagreb performance of Conway the Machine. A traditional expression of thanks to the sponsors followed, along with an invitation to viewers to support the podcast via Patreon in order to raise funds for new video equipment, and with the recognizable greeting and friendly fist bump, a finishing touch was put on yet another content-rich episode.
